taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Oct 24, 2026 is indeed a Saturday, so "six days from today" is Friday, Oct 30, and the deadline is Oct 30 at 11:59 PM PT.

**Time zones on that date:**
- The US is still on daylight time until Nov 1, so Pacific time is PDT (UTC−7).
- The EU ended daylight time on Oct 25, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**Conversion:** Oct 30, 23:59 PDT is Oct 31, 06:59 UTC, which is Oct 31, 07:59 in Madrid. The difference is 8 hours, not the usual 9, because the EU clock change comes a week before the US one.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The page's date checks out: October 30, 2026 is a Friday, so "this coming Monday" is November 2, 2026.

Daylight saving time matters here:
- Europe ended DST on October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
- The US ends DST on Sunday, November 1, 2026, so by Monday Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8).

The time difference on that Monday is 9 hours. So 10:00 AM in Los Angeles is 19:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2), which is 16:00 UTC.

Daylight saving time ends in Spain on Sunday, October 25, 2026, when clocks go back from 03:00 to 02:00. That day has 25 hours, so 48 real hours after the start falls one hour later on the clock than you might expect.

48 hours after 16:00 UTC on Oct 24 is 16:00 UTC on Monday, October 26. Madrid is then on CET (UTC+1), so the local time is 17:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Start time:** On October 26, 2026, Pacific Time is still on daylight time (PDT, UTC-7), because the US clocks don't change until November 1. So 10:00 AM PDT is 17:00 UTC.

**Deadline:** 72 hours later is October 29, 2026 at 17:00 UTC. No clock changes fall in between.

**Madrid time:** Spain's daylight saving time ended on October 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). 17:00 UTC is therefore 18:00 in Madrid.

The deadline is Thursday, October 29, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Convert the close time.** Oct 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET is still daylight time (EDT, UTC‑4), because US DST ends on Nov 1, 2026. That is Nov 1, 03:59 UTC.

**Add 36 hours.** This gives Nov 2, 15:59 UTC. The US clocks change in between, but "exactly 36 hours" means elapsed time, so that doesn't affect the result.

**Convert to Madrid.** Spain's DST ended on Oct 25, 2026, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). That makes it Nov 2, 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The timestamp 1791788340 converts as follows:

- 1791788340 s ÷ 86400 = 20738 days plus 25140 s. That is day 20738 after 1970-01-01, at 06:59:00 UTC.
- Day 20738 is 2026-10-12. Check: 2026-01-01 is day 20454, and 20738 − 20454 = 284 days later, which lands on October 12.
- So the deadline is 2026-10-12 06:59 UTC.
- Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9 with no daylight saving, so add 9 hours: 15:59 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 2026-10-25 02:30 UTC.

Madrid uses Central European Time (UTC+1) in winter and Central European Summer Time (UTC+2) in summer. In 2026, daylight saving time ends on Sunday, 25 October, at 01:00 UTC, when clocks go back from 03:00 to 02:00 local time.

The deadline at 02:30 UTC falls after that switch, so Madrid is on UTC+1. That makes the local time 03:30.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25 (October 1 is a Thursday, so the Sundays are the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th).

- US daylight saving time doesn't end until November 1, so on October 25 Pacific Time is still PDT (UTC-7). 11:59 PM PDT is 06:59 UTC on October 26.
- Europe's daylight saving time ends on October 25 at 01:00 UTC, so by October 26 Madrid is on CET (UTC+1). 06:59 UTC is 07:59 in Madrid.

The deadline falls on Monday morning, October 26, at 07:59 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday (Nov 1, 2026: let me verify. Jan 1, 2026 is Thursday. Nov 1 is day 305; (305-1) = 304 days after Jan 1; 304 mod 7 = 3; Thursday + 3 = Sunday. Yes).

So DST ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at 2:00 a.m. local time. At 12:00 noon that day, Eastern Time is already back on standard time (EST, UTC−5).

Lima, Peru is on UTC−5 year-round (no DST).

So 12:00 noon EST = 12:00 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC−12. "December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE" is the end of December 31 in UTC−12, which is January 1, 2027, 00:00 at UTC−12.

Converting to UTC: add 12 hours, giving 2027-01-01 12:00 UTC.

Tokyo is UTC+9 (JST, no daylight saving), so add 9 hours: 2027-01-01 21:00 JST.

The deadline in Tokyo is 9:00 PM on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Sydney:** Daylight saving time in Sydney starts on the first Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 4. So on October 5 Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11), and 5:00 PM there is 06:00 UTC.

**New York:** New York is still on daylight time (EDT, UTC−4) until November 1. So 06:00 UTC is 2:00 AM in New York on October 5.

Since you're in New York that week and want New York time, the deadline is 2:00 AM on October 5, 2026. For reference, Madrid would be 08:00 that morning (CEST, UTC+2).

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
